I think the whole discussion is whether a sub is private or public.

For me, the ideal is that each sub should get a share from the economic profit of the site. But in order to do that you have to abide to the "Voat Constitution". If you do that, your sub become "default". The rules can be whatever, but at the same time, your mod lost all their power and they are there just to delete totally offtopic messages, unmarked spoilers, and so on. A mod should be but a represent of the user base; that why I think mods for public subs should be changing at random every now and then, and grant them very little power.

Any Internet forum cannot function for long if there isn't some kind of moderation.

Forums have been around since the birth of the Internet. Trust me, we've experimented.

the closest we have to a popular space online with freespeech is 8chan (4chan has had too many corrupted modding in recent yrs), hopefully this site'll remain as free as it supposedly is now. The supposed idea about corrupt mods is this power-to-the-people mantra of how if a sub is modded badly an alt is set up, hopefully this site can cope in a way similar- as the fact is that there will be dumb mods, just hopefully dumb admins

I'm not sure exactly when this free speech mantra started, but the time I heard it most was when we had people wanting to post pictures of their spouses after having beaten them up, or wanting to peruse pictures of children in a subverse where there was discussion on where to see "more".

Having been a moderator on a game server I can say with certainty that moderation is necessary. When the mods are absent things turn to shit. Even on places like reddit moderation is necessary, but it depends on the specific subreddit as to how involved the moderation should be. For example, on /r/Morrowind I barely do any moderation, but we recently had a mild influx of silly posts from /r/truestl with brigade like posts having been made. People who were regular members of our community were sending us mail about it, so we removed the posts and contacted the mods of the other subreddit, had a good chat, and both communities are happy now.

The people who will be predisposed to never be happy unless they are making others unhappy are the trolls, the people with antisocial personality disorder, or malignant narcissism. These folks scream bloody murder and free speech when any moderation takes place.

The thing to remember is that it's called moderation, as in moderate, as in not extreme. It isn't a slippery slope to widespread censorship to have a public servant responsible for maintaining order. If this were so then police would be tyrants 100% of the time, nobody would be served by the government, everyone would know that anarchy is best, etc.

This does not mean that moderators are always good or that police and governments never do bad things. Indeed there are instances of misconduct for all three authorities. This is why it I's important to have checks and balances, things like moderation logs, or the possibility to replace moderators, citizens rights advocates and watchdogs like the aclu and amnesty international, jury nullification, etc. For those times when moderators or police forget why they are granted authority and abuse it for purposes that no longer serve the community.

I would rather see a moderation log with entries where trolling and spam have been removed than an empty one.

edit: typos

I definitely think it's needed, specially for subs with very specific content. For example, subs dedicated to recipes and cooking should not have to deal with everyone getting pissy that they're deleting threads about politics.

However, if a sub has rules that allows it to be about free asking, then the moderation should only really be related to spam, theats and doxxing.
